cards.text: King Saul is dead, and all Israel comes together to David son of Jesse at Hebron. ALL of them, at one man's door. Friend, the biggest crowd I ever saw in that junk drawer was me and three rubber bands.

cards.question: At Hebron, the people of Israel tell David they're his own flesh and blood.

cards.text: Then they remind David that even while Saul was king, David was the one who led Israel out and brought them back. Friend, they're reading the man his own résumé.

cards.question: The people also remind David what the LORD his God said he would be for Israel. What picture does the LORD use?

cards.text: So all the elders of Israel come to the king at Hebron. Friend, this just went from the group chat to the MEETING.

cards.question: At Hebron, David makes a ___ with the elders of Israel before the LORD.
Then the elders of Israel make David king over Israel. How do they do it?
David being anointed king over Israel happens according to the word of the LORD through Samuel the prophet.

cards.text: Now David and all the Israelites march to Jerusalem. Back then it's called Jebus, and the Jebusites live in the land.

cards.question: When David and the Israelites arrive, what do the people of Jebus tell him?

answers.text: You will never get in here
Come in and be our king

cards.question: The people of Jebus manage to keep David out of the fortress of Zion.

cards.text: "You will never get in here." Friend, I said that to the dust in the drawer every day. The dust got in. Now, before all this, David had made his men an offer about whoever is first to strike down a Jebusite.

cards.question: What does David say the first man to strike down a Jebusite will get?

answers.text: He gets a city of his own

cards.question: ___ son of Zeruiah goes up first, and he becomes the chief.

cards.text: Joab hears "chief commander" and he is UP there. No interview. No follow-up email. GONE.

cards.question: David takes up residence in the fortress, and that's why it's called the City of ___.

cards.text: Then David builds up the city around the fortress, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall. He didn't just move in, friend. He's RENOVATING.

cards.question: While David builds up the city around the fortress, Joab restores the rest of the city.

cards.text: And from here, David becomes greater and greater. Me? I've been the same size since the Millers' kitchen, and the gold base only adds about an inch.

cards.question: Why does David become greater and greater?

answers.text: The LORD of Hosts is with him

findings.problem: The card says King Saul is dead and calls David 'son of Jesse.' Both facts come from outside the passage (1 Chronicles 10:13-14), but the card cites only 1 Chronicles 11:1, so they have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card says David 'made his men an offer.' Verse 6 only says 'Now David had said,' and never says who he said it to. The card adds an audience the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says 'Joab hears "chief commander" and he is UP there,' which makes the reward the reason Joab went up first. Verse 6 only says Joab went up first and became chief. It gives no reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to verse 6, which cards 12 to 14 already covered. It tells nothing new and doesn't move the passage forward. The joke has no new piece of the passage to ride along on.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: In verse 9, David 'becomes greater and greater' in standing and power. The joke compares this to Papa Dorin's physical size and the height of his gold base. That is a different action, so the comparison doesn't match.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The LORD of Hosts is with him,' uses a Bible title. The wrong answers, 'His army keeps getting bigger' and 'The Jebusites start serving him,' sound plain and modern. The right answer stands out as the one that sounds like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
